title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Directors, the Company Secretary, the CEO, the CEO's direct reports (Senior Executive team), direct reports of the Senior Executive team, and other persons nominated by the Company Secretary. All substantive prohibitions (closed periods, prior notification, hedging/derivatives ban, margin loan ban, secured financing approval, short selling and short-term dealing) apply to this tier.

tiers.name: Employees
tiers.description: All employees within the nib Group; only the parts of the policy specifically identified apply to them (confidentiality of information, possible extension to related-company securities, annual acknowledgement), plus the insider trading ban which applies to everyone at all times.

tiers.name: Associates
tiers.description: A spouse or partner; a child or step-child under 18; a relative sharing the same household for 12+ months; an entity of which the KMP is a director/secretary/officer (absent an information wall); a company in which the KMP holds or controls at least 20%; a trust of which the KMP or specified family are beneficiaries; and any other person over whom the KMP has or may be expected to have investment control or influence. The KMP must obtain clearance and notify on their Associates' behalf.

definitions.hedging_definition: products associated with NHF Securities which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in NHF (eg hedging arrangements)

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the date two weeks before 31 December each year
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the half-year results announcement is released to the market following lodgement with ASX

windows.start_anchor: close of trading on the date two weeks before 30 June each year
windows.end_anchor: 24 hours after the annual results announcement is released to the market following lodgement with ASX

windows.start_anchor: 28 days before the annual general meeting
windows.end_anchor: start of trading on the first trading day after the annual general meeting

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: Board of Directors may specify an extension to a Closed Period, or an additional Closed Period; confidentiality is not addressed.

rules.detail: Absolute, unconditional ban 'at any time' on dealing in options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over NHF Securities by third parties such as banks; no closed-period, notification or approval route applies to this Part 4 prohibition (distinct from the Part 3 dealing regime). Does not extend to secured financing arrangements under 4.3.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel and their Associates are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products designed to track, hedge or in any other way take a position associated with the future value of NHF Securities, including options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over NHF Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions.

rules.detail: General ban on transactions in products associated with NHF Securities that limit the economic risk of a KMP's or Associate's security holding, expressly extended to any hedging arrangement over incentive plan rights, and specifically to unvested or vested-but-holding-locked remuneration. A put option on incentive remuneration and a short position are given as named prohibited examples.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel and their Associates are not permitted to enter into transactions in products associated with NHF Securities which operate to limit the economic risk of their security holding in NHF (eg hedging arrangements). ... Examples of prohibited arrangements: a put option on incentive remuneration

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but a prepaid forward or similar structured sale to a bank counterparty is a financial product taking a position associated with the future value of NHF Securities issued by a third-party institution, and so falls within the absolute 4.1 ban.
rules.evidence: financial products designed to track, hedge or in any other way take a position associated with the future value of NHF Securities, including options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over NHF Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions.

rules.detail: Outright ban on short selling NHF Securities; nib separately states it encourages KMP to be long-term investors.
rules.evidence: Key Management Persons and their Associates must not engage in short selling of NHF Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the policy.
CFDs are not named, but as a financial product issued by a bank or institution taking a position associated with the future value of NHF Securities, a CFD falls within the absolute 4.1 ban.
rules.evidence: financial products designed to track, hedge or in any other way take a position associated with the future value of NHF Securities, including options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over NHF Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions.

rules.detail: Outright, unconditional ban on entering into or maintaining a margin loan over NHF Securities, with no Board approval route (contrast with other secured financial arrangements).
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel and their Associates are prohibited from entering into or maintaining a margin loan over NHF Securities.

rules.detail: Encumbering NHF Securities to secure financing (other than a margin loan) is expressly permitted subject to Board approval.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel and their Associates are permitted to enter into or maintain other secured financial arrangements over NHF Securities subject to Board approval being obtained.

rules.detail: Secured financing arrangements over NHF Securities other than margin loans are expressly permitted with Board approval; margin loans specifically remain prohibited outright.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel and their Associates are permitted to enter into or maintain other secured financial arrangements over NHF Securities subject to Board approval being obtained.

rules.detail: Ban on short-term or speculative trading in NHF Securities or in derivative or other financial products issued over or in respect of NHF Securities, defined as a term of less than 6 months.
rules.evidence: Key Management Persons and their Associates must not engage in short term or speculative trading in NHF Securities or in derivative or other financial products issued over or in respect of NHF Securities. Short term means a term of less than a 6 month period.

clearance.approver: Notification Officer per Schedule 2: Chair for the Managing Director/CEO and for Non-Executive Directors; Managing Director or Chair of the Audit Committee for the Chair; Managing Director for the Company Secretary; Company Secretary for all other Key Management Personnel
clearance.post_trade_deadline: no later than 2 working days after the dealing
clearance.evidence: A confirmation allowing a dealing expires 5 days from its date, unless it specifies a different expiry date. ... Key Management Personnel or their Associates ... must confirm in writing to the relevant Notification Officer(s) when the dealing in NHF Securities has occurred, the number of NHF Securities affected and the relevant parties to the dealing, no later than 2 working days after the dealing in NHF Securities has occurred.

short_term.basis: term of the trading, not from acquisition
short_term.evidence: Key Management Persons and their Associates must not engage in short term or speculative trading in NHF Securities or in derivative or other financial products issued over or in respect of NHF Securities. Short term means a term of less than a 6 month period.

exceptions.evidence: severe financial hardship, for example, a pressing financial commitment that cannot be satisfied otherwise than by selling the relevant NHF Securities
requirements under a court order or court enforceable undertakings or other legal or regulatory requirements

exceptions.approver: Chair of the Board (or Chair of the Audit Committee where the Chair of the Board is involved)
exceptions.evidence: other exceptional circumstances as determined by the Chair of the Board (or Chair of the Audit Committee where the Chair of the Board is involved).
(lender disposal) a disposal of NHF Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights;

(trading plan) trading under a non-discretionary trading plan for which prior written clearance has been provided in accordance with procedures set out in this policy ... the trading plan does not permit the Key Management Person or their Associate to exercise any influence or discretion over how, when, or whether to trade.

(rights offers, SPPs and DRPs and buy-backs) trading under an offer or invitation made to all or most of the security holders, such as a rights issue, a security purchase plan, a dividend or distribution reinvestment plan and an equal access buy-back
(takeover) undertakings to accept, or the acceptance of, a takeover offer;
(incentive scheme) the exercise (but not the sale of NHF Securities following exercise) of an option or right under an employee incentive scheme
(superannuation) transfers of securities which are already held in a superannuation fund or other saving scheme in which the Key Management Person or their Associate is a beneficiary

exemption_authority: No exemption route exists for the Part 4 prohibitions (third-party derivatives/hedging, margin loans, short selling, short-term trading) - they apply 'at any time' with no waiver mechanism identified. Within Part 3, the Notification Officer (or the Chair of the Board/Audit Committee for other exceptional circumstances) may permit dealing during a Closed Period only for defined exceptional circumstances, and any such approval 'must be obtained in advance, cannot be given after the event and will be final and binding.'
jurisdiction_overlays: ASX Listing Rules and ASX Guidance Note 27 (exceptional circumstances determination)
Corporations Act 2001 (Cth) insider trading and substantial shareholding notification provisions

bespoke_clauses.topic: third-party derivative ban has no exemption route
bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel and their Associates are not permitted to deal at any time in financial products designed to track, hedge or in any other way take a position associated with the future value of NHF Securities, including options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over NHF Securities by third parties such as banks and other institutions.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is an absolute, unconditional ban on buying options (including puts) or other derivatives from a bank counterparty over NHF shares; unlike the Part 3 closed-period regime it carries no exceptional-circumstances or Board-approval carve-out, so the option legs of a funded collar cannot be cleared under any provision of this policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Examples of prohibited arrangements: a put option on incentive remuneration
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The policy names a put option specifically as an example of a prohibited hedging arrangement, directly capturing the purchased-put leg of a collar.

bespoke_clauses.topic: secured financing permitted with Board approval
bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel and their Associates are permitted to enter into or maintain other secured financial arrangements over NHF Securities subject to Board approval being obtained.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike margin loans, a loan secured on the collared shares (not itself a margin loan) could in principle proceed with Board approval, but this is moot while the option legs remain absolutely prohibited by paragraph 4.1.

bespoke_clauses.clause: (lender disposal) a disposal of NHF Securities that is the result of a secured lender exercising their rights;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: If a secured facility were ever put in place, the lender's enforcement sale is excluded from the closed-period/notification regime (though still subject to the insider trading ban), so enforcement is not itself a breach.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Notification of any dealing in NHF Securities under this paragraph and the completion of Part B of the Notification Form to Deal in NHF Securities does not constitute approval of the dealing by or on behalf of the nib Group.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside closed periods the KMP self-certifies via notification rather than obtaining company approval, so nib bears no responsibility for clearing the collar's timing even when the process is followed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Any such approval must be obtained in advance, cannot be given after the event and will be final and binding on the applicant. No reasons are required to be given for any decision regarding whether or not to provide an approval.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Even if the derivative ban were waived, closed-period execution of the collar would require discretionary, unreasoned and unappealable approval obtained strictly in advance.

summary: A funded collar is not possible under this policy for Key Management Personnel or their Associates. Paragraph 4.1 imposes an absolute, carve-out-free ban on dealing 'at any time' in options, warrants, futures or other financial products issued over NHF Securities by third parties such as banks, which catches both the purchased put and written call legs of an OTC collar; paragraph 4.2 separately names 'a put option on incentive remuneration' as a prohibited hedging arrangement and more broadly bans transactions limiting the economic risk of a KMP's security holding. The loan leg is not entirely closed off: margin loans over NHF Securities are prohibited outright, but 'other secured financial arrangements' over NHF Securities are expressly permitted subject to Board approval, so a loan secured on the shares could in principle be approved on its own. A secured lender's enforcement sale, if it ever occurred, is a Schedule 4 excluded dealing outside the Closed Period/notification regime, though always subject to the insider trading ban. Because the option components have no approval or exceptional-circumstances route anywhere in the policy, the collar as a whole cannot be implemented notwithstanding the more permissive secured-financing provision.
